idea.body: Adding and subtracting big numbers both work one place at a time, starting from the ones. Addition sometimes needs a carry: when a column totals 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry the rest into the next column. Subtraction sometimes needs a borrow: when the top digit is smaller than the bottom one, borrow a ten from the next column over. A rover's log showing 3,482 plus 2,159 needs one carry to reach 5,641. That same log showing 5,000 minus 2,387 needs several borrows in a row, since every digit after the 5 starts as a zero.

workedExample.prompt: A workshop had 5,000 bolts. It used 2,387 of them. How many bolts are left?
steps: Line up 5,000 and 2,387 by place value.
The ones column needs to borrow, but the tens, hundreds and thousands columns are all zero, so the borrow chains back to the 5.
The 5 becomes a 4, and every zero along the way becomes a 9, except the ones place, which becomes 10.
Now subtract each column: 10 minus 7 is 3, 9 minus 8 is 1, 9 minus 3 is 6, 4 minus 2 is 2.
That gives 2,613 bolts left.

ways.name: Column method with carrying
ways.when: Use this for any multi-digit addition or subtraction, with room to line up columns.
steps: Line up 3,482 and 2,159 by place value, ones under ones.
Add the ones: 2 plus 9 is 11, write 1, carry 1.
Add the tens: 8 plus 5 plus the carried 1 is 14, write 4, carry 1.
Add the hundreds: 4 plus 1 plus the carried 1 is 6.
Add the thousands: 3 plus 2 is 5.
The total is 5,641.
ways.trap: Forgetting to add the carried 1 into the next column.

ways.name: Round and adjust
ways.when: Use this when one number sits close to a round number.
steps: Round 398 up to 400, an easier number to add.
Add the rounded number: 400 plus 256 is 656.
398 is 2 less than 400, so 2 extra got added.
Subtract that 2 back off: 656 minus 2 is 654.
ways.trap: Rounding the number but forgetting to adjust the answer back at the end.

ways.name: Counting up in jumps
ways.when: Use this for subtraction, especially when the two numbers sit far apart.
steps: Start at the smaller number, 2,387.
Jump to a friendly number: add 13 to reach 2,400.
Jump in a big round step: add 600 to reach 3,000.
Jump the rest of the way: add 2,000 to reach 5,000.
Add the jumps: 13 plus 600 plus 2,000 is 2,613.
ways.trap: Losing track of one jump and leaving it out of the final sum.

figure.alt: Three jump boxes from 2,387 to 5,000: plus 13, plus 600, plus 2,000, totalling 2,613.

frames.caption: Jump to a friendly number: add 13.
Jump a big round step: add 600.
Jump the rest of the way: +2,000.

ways.name: Partial sums
ways.when: Use this for addition when you would rather not carry as you go.
steps: Break each number into place-value parts: 456 is 400 plus 50 plus 6.
382 is 300 plus 80 plus 2.
Add the hundreds parts: 400 plus 300 is 700.
Add the tens parts: 50 plus 80 is 130.
Add the ones parts: 6 plus 2 is 8.
Add the three partial sums: 700 plus 130 plus 8 is 838.
ways.trap: Forgetting to add all the partial sums together at the end.
